newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-HODGSON EXPECTS A DIFFERENT INTER AGAINST SCHALKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODGSON EXPECTS A DIFFERENT INTER AGAINST SCHALKE.

text.p: Inter Milan's English coach Roy Hodgson says his team, lacklustre at Roma on Sunday, will be very different in their UEFA Cup final second leg match against Germany's Schalke on Wednesday.
"Today there was something on the players' minds that stopped them being aggressive and sharp," he said after the 1-1 draw at the weekend.
"Before the match, we talked of winning it but, once on the pitch, I think all of the players concentrated on not picking up an injury (before) Wednesday's final.
"In the end, we were lucky to get a draw here and it's obvious that Inter could have done a lot better."
Inter go into the second leg at San Siro trailing by one goal but Hodgson believes his side will raise their game for the occasion.
"On Wednesday night I want to see them chase more, get more stuck in. That's why I think you'll see an entirely different Inter against Shalke."
For the final, Inter have back three key players who missed the first leg through suspension -- French defender Jocelyn Angloma, English midfielder Paul Ince and Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff.
Djorkaeff replaces Dutchman Aron Winter while Ince's return to midfield will probably see Salvatore Fresi move back again to a central defensive position in place of suspended Fabio Galante.
Angloma may replace either Alessandro Pistone or Giuseppe Bergomi in a full back role.
Inter's 20-year-old Nigerian star Nwankwo Kanu, recovering from heart surgery to resolve a problem which threatened to prematurely end his career, will be a spectator.
Kanu, who joined Inter last year from Dutch side Ajax Amsterdam but was ruled out of competitive soccer on the eve of the season, has been given the go-ahead to resume playing by his doctors.
He is expected to resume training with Inter this summer in preparation for a possible comeback in the autumn.
